title: Cartesian section morphisms extend uniquely from a locally covering subsieve
statement:
Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-topos] small in the larger universe, and let $\mathcal Q$ be a category fibred in groupoids with fibre objects and arrows in that universe. Assume that $\mathcal Q$ is a prestack: for every $V$ and $a,b\in\mathcal Q(V)$, the presheaf on $\mathcal C/V$ assigning to $h:W\to V$ the set $\operatorname{Isom}(h^*a,h^*b)$ is a sheaf for the induced topology (a sieve on an object $h:W\to V$ covers exactly when its underlying sieve on $W$ belongs to $J(W)$). For a sieve $S$ on $T$, let $\operatorname{Sec}_{\mathcal Q}(S)$ be the groupoid of cartesian sections over its full subcategory of $\mathcal C/T$: objects are families $x_f\in\mathcal Q(\operatorname{dom}f)$ with coherent isomorphisms $h^*x_f\cong x_{fh}$, and arrows are families of fibre isomorphisms commuting with these comparisons. Let $K\subseteq S$ be sieves on $T$, not necessarily covering $T$, and suppose $f^*K\in J(V)$ for every $f:V\to T$ in $S$. Then for any $x,y\in\operatorname{Sec}_{\mathcal Q}(S)$, restriction is a bijection
$$\operatorname{Isom}_{\operatorname{Sec}_{\mathcal Q}(S)}(x,y)\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;\operatorname{Isom}_{\operatorname{Sec}_{\mathcal Q}(K)}(x|_K,y|_K).$$
Equivalently, restriction of cartesian sections from $S$ to $K$ is fully faithful.

source.place: Tag 02ZN (lemma-stackify), naive proof, final construction checks (4) and (8); less naive proof, morphisms on refinements. The locally covering sieve formulation is the descent-of-morphisms argument underlying those checks.

proof.text:
Let $\alpha:x|_K\to y|_K$ be an arrow. Write $c^x_{f,h}:h^*x_f\xrightarrow{\sim}x_{fh}$ and $c^y_{f,h}$ for the transition isomorphisms. For $f:V\to T$ in $S$ and $h:W\to V$ with $fh\in K$, put
$$b_{f,h}=(c^y_{f,h})^{-1}\alpha_{fh}c^x_{f,h}\in\operatorname{Isom}(h^*x_f,h^*y_f).$$
Composition is read right to left. For any $k:Z\to W$, the sieve property gives $fhk\in K$. Naturality of $\alpha$ says $\alpha_{fhk}c^x_{fh,k}=c^y_{fh,k}k^*\alpha_{fh}$. Substituting this in the formula for $b_{f,hk}$ and using the coherence identities $c^x_{f,hk}=c^x_{fh,k}k^*c^x_{f,h}$ and the same identity for $y$ gives $b_{f,hk}=k^*b_{f,h}$. These equalities include the canonical comparison $(hk)^*\cong k^*h^*$; they are identities in that common parenthesization, not an assumption of strict pullbacks. Thus $(b_{f,h})_{h\in f^*K}$ is a matching family in the isomorphism presheaf for $x_f,y_f$ on $\mathcal C/V$.

source.place: Tag 02ZN, lemma-stackify, naive proof final checks (4) and (8), and less naive proof morphisms on refinements; the following supplies the omitted descent-of-morphisms check using Sites Tag 00Z8 (definition-sheaf-sets-topology).

proof.text:
For each $f:V\to T$ in $S$, take the sieve on $1_V$ in $\mathcal C/V$ consisting of the arrows $h\to1_V$ with $h\in f^*K$. It covers: its underlying sieve is $f^*K\in J(V)$ by the hypothesis. The isomorphism presheaf for $x_f,y_f$ is a sheaf by the prestack hypothesis. Apply exactly the unique-amalgamation clause of [def-weil-pbc-topos] to the matching family from step 1. Its unique amalgamation, identified using the unit pullback isomorphisms, is
$$\beta_f:x_f\xrightarrow{\sim}y_f,\qquad h^*\beta_f=b_{f,h}\quad(h\in f^*K).$$
There is no descent of objects here: $x_f,y_f$ are already given, and we glue elements of their stated isomorphism sheaf. The index sets are in the fixed larger universe because the site and its fibre arrows are.

source.place: Tag 02ZN, lemma-stackify, naive proof final checks (4) and (8), and less naive proof morphisms on refinements; the following supplies the omitted descent-of-morphisms check using Sites Tag 00Z8 (definition-sheaf-sets-topology).

proof.text:
The family $\beta$ is compatible with every section transition. Indeed, let $h:W\to V$ with $f\in S$, so $fh\in S$. Compare in $\operatorname{Isom}(x_{fh},y_{fh})$ the two elements $\beta_{fh}$ and
$$\gamma=c^y_{f,h}(h^*\beta_f)(c^x_{f,h})^{-1}.$$
For any $k:Z\to W$ with $fhk\in K$, the gluing formulas give
$$k^*\gamma=(k^*c^y_{f,h})b_{f,hk}(k^*c^x_{f,h})^{-1}=(c^y_{fh,k})^{-1}\alpha_{fhk}c^x_{fh,k}=k^*\beta_{fh}.$$
The middle equality is obtained by substituting $b_{f,hk}$ and cancelling the two factors $k^*c_{f,h}$ using the same coherence identities as in step 1. As $(fh)^*K\in J(W)$, unique amalgamation for the isomorphism sheaf of $x_{fh},y_{fh}$, as defined in [def-weil-pbc-topos], implies $\gamma=\beta_{fh}$. This is exactly $\beta_{fh}c^x_{f,h}=c^y_{f,h}h^*\beta_f$. Thus $\beta$ is an arrow of cartesian sections; its pointwise inverses satisfy the inverse equation, hence it is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 02ZN, lemma-stackify, naive proof final checks (4) and (8), and less naive proof morphisms on refinements; the following supplies the omitted descent-of-morphisms check using Sites Tag 00Z8 (definition-sheaf-sets-topology).

proof.text:
If $f\in K$, then $1_V\in f^*K$. The gluing equation at $h=1_V$ gives $\beta_f=\alpha_f$, after the section unit comparison isomorphisms. Consequently $\beta|_K=\alpha$, proving surjectivity of restriction. If $\delta,\epsilon:x\to y$ have the same restriction to $K$, then for each $f\in S$ and each $h\in f^*K$, their compatibility with $c^x,c^y$ gives
$$h^*\delta_f=(c^y_{f,h})^{-1}\delta_{fh}c^x_{f,h}=(c^y_{f,h})^{-1}\epsilon_{fh}c^x_{f,h}=h^*\epsilon_f.$$
The uniqueness clause of [def-weil-pbc-topos] for the same covering sieve on $1_V$ gives $\delta_f=\epsilon_f$ for every $f$, so $\delta=\epsilon$. This proves injectivity and hence the asserted bijection for every $x,y$. Since all arrows in the section categories are invertible, these are their entire Hom sets, proving full faithfulness.
